questions.q: In early Tamil sources, which three dynasties were collectively called the Muvendar?
questions.e: Muvendar refers to the three crowned kings of early Tamilakam: the Cholas, Cheras and Pandyas. Sangam poems and related early Tamil sources describe their territories, rivalries and patronage; the term does not refer to later northern dynasties.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Kerala SCERT, Standard VI Social Science Part II — Sangam Age.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Kerala SCERT, Standard VI Social Science Part II — Sangam Age

questions.q: What did the Kudavolai method in Chola village administration refer to?
o: A hereditary system for appointing the village headman
A land-revenue assessment based on crop rotation
A ballot-based method used to select members of village committees
A military levy collected from coastal merchants
questions.e: Kudavolai is associated with Chola-period village self-government and the selection of committee members through a ballot or ticket procedure. It illustrates local administration; it was not a hereditary appointment, a land tax or a military levy.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Tamil Nadu Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department — village self-government reference.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Tamil Nadu Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department — village self-government reference

questions.q: In the Vijayanagara Empire, what was the main obligation of an amara-nayaka who received an amaram territory?
o: Maintain troops and remit dues while administering the assigned territory
Serve only as a temple priest
Collect customs duty exclusively at seaports
Act as the emperor's ambassador to foreign courts
questions.e: Amara-nayakas were military chiefs who held assigned territories called amaram. They collected revenue, maintained troops and fulfilled obligations to the Vijayanagara ruler; the position combined territorial administration with military service.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT, Themes in Indian History II — Vijayanagara chapter.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT, Themes in Indian History II — Vijayanagara chapter

questions.q: Which description best captures a paik in the Ahom kingdom?
o: A hereditary temple accountant exempt from state duties
A foreign merchant who paid customs but no land dues
A cavalry commander paid only in cash
An adult male liable for compulsory civil and military service, often serving as peasant, soldier or labourer
questions.e: Under the Ahom paik system, adult male subjects were organised for compulsory service to the state. A paik could be mobilised for labour or military duty, linking the kingdom's manpower organisation with its administration and defence.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Archaeological Survey of India, Guwahati Circle — The Military System of the Ahoms.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Archaeological Survey of India, Guwahati Circle — The Military System of the Ahoms

questions.q: What was a khanqah in the medieval Sufi tradition?
o: A tax office attached to a market
A hospice or centre where a Sufi master and disciples lived and met
A military camp used by cavalry
questions.e: A khanqah was a Sufi hospice or residential centre associated with a spiritual master and disciples. It provided a setting for instruction, devotional gatherings and community life; it was not a treasury, tax office or army camp.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT, Our Pasts II — devotional and Sufi traditions chapter.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT, Our Pasts II — devotional and Sufi traditions chapter

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) from the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)?
o: CRR is held only in gold; SLR is held only as cash with RBI
CRR is maintained as cash balances with RBI; SLR is maintained in specified liquid assets
Both are deposits that banks place with the Finance Ministry
CRR applies to borrowers; SLR applies only to exporters
questions.e: CRR is the prescribed share of a bank's net demand and time liabilities maintained as a cash balance with the Reserve Bank. SLR is maintained by the bank itself in prescribed liquid assets such as cash, gold and eligible securities, so the two requirements are not interchangeable.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Reserve Bank of India — Cash Reserve Ratio and Statutory Liquidity Ratio directions.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India — Cash Reserve Ratio and Statutory Liquidity Ratio directions

questions.q: When the RBI purchases government securities outright through an open-market operation, what is the immediate liquidity effect on the banking system?
o: Liquidity is absorbed from the banking system
The money supply is automatically reduced to zero
The transaction has no effect on banking-system liquidity
Liquidity is injected into the banking system
questions.e: An outright RBI purchase of government securities pays funds into the banking system and increases reserves or liquidity. A sale has the opposite direction and absorbs funds. The question asks about a purchase, so the immediate effect is an injection.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Reserve Bank of India — Monetary Policy Instruments and liquidity management.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India — Monetary Policy Instruments and liquidity management

questions.q: In the RBI's liquidity framework, the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) primarily allows the Reserve Bank to:
o: Absorb overnight liquidity from eligible participants without providing collateral
Lend long-term project finance directly to companies
Guarantee deposits held by cooperative societies
Purchase foreign currency only from exporters
questions.e: The SDF is a collateral-free facility through which eligible participants can place overnight funds with the RBI. It helps the Reserve Bank absorb surplus liquidity and operates as the floor of the liquidity adjustment facility corridor.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Reserve Bank of India — Monetary Policy Instruments and liquidity management.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India — Monetary Policy Instruments and liquidity management

questions.q: In India's monetary statistics, which combination constitutes M1, or narrow money?
o: Currency with the public + all time deposits with banks + post-office term deposits
Only notes and coins held by the public
Currency with the public + demand deposits with the banking system + other deposits with RBI
Currency in circulation + banks' cash balances + government securities
questions.e: M1 is the narrow-money measure: currency with the public, demand deposits with the banking system and other deposits with the RBI. Time deposits with banks are added when calculating M3, so they are not part of M1.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Reserve Bank of India — Monetary Aggregates, M1 and M3 definitions.

questions.q: In the Self-Help Group (SHG)-bank linkage model, which feature helps members who may not individually possess conventional collateral obtain formal credit?
o: A government guarantee of every member's private debt
Regular group savings and collective responsibility for deciding and repaying loans
A requirement that every member own agricultural land
A rule that banks lend only to the group leader
questions.e: SHG members save regularly into a common fund and decide loans collectively. Group records, peer monitoring and shared repayment responsibility help banks assess the group and can widen access to formal credit for members who lack individual collateral.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT Class X Economics — Money and Credit chapter.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT Class X Economics — Money and Credit chapter

questions.q: A bank reports total credit of ₹720 crore and total deposits of ₹900 crore. What is its credit-deposit ratio?
questions.e: Credit-deposit ratio = total credit divided by total deposits, multiplied by 100. Here 720 ÷ 900 = 0.8, and 0.8 × 100 = 80%. It indicates the proportion of deposit resources deployed as credit.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Reserve Bank of India — Banking and monetary statistics, credit-deposit ratio.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India — Banking and monetary statistics, credit-deposit ratio

questions.q: A student can see nearby objects clearly, but distant objects appear blurred. Which lens is normally used to correct this defect?
questions.e: Myopia, or short-sightedness, causes distant objects to focus in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens spreads incoming rays before they enter the eye and shifts the focus back onto the retina.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT Class X Science — Human Eye and the Colourful World.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT Class X Science — Human Eye and the Colourful World

questions.q: In a Mendelian monohybrid cross between two heterozygous tall pea plants, what phenotypic ratio is expected in the F2 generation if tallness is completely dominant?
questions.e: In a Tt × Tt cross, the genotypic ratio is 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt. With complete dominance, TT and Tt are tall while tt is dwarf, producing the 3:1 phenotypic ratio.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT Class X Science — Heredity chapter.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT Class X Science — Heredity chapter

questions.q: The production of an electric current in a coil when the magnetic flux linked with it changes is called:
questions.e: Faraday's law states that a changing magnetic flux through a coil induces an electromotive force. In an electric generator, relative motion between the coil and magnetic field changes the flux and produces current.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT Class X Science — Magnetic Effects of Electric Current.

questions.topic: Plant Physiology — Guard Cells and Stomata
questions.q: Which specialised cells regulate the opening and closing of stomatal pores in leaves?
questions.e: Guard cells are specialised cells that flank each stomatal pore. Changes in their turgor pressure open or close the pore, regulating carbon-dioxide entry for photosynthesis and water-vapour loss through transpiration.
tags: Plant Physiology — Guard Cells and Stomata

questions.q: Which mode of heat transfer can occur through a vacuum without requiring a material medium?
questions.e: Radiation transfers energy by electromagnetic waves and does not require matter. This is why heat from the Sun can cross the near-vacuum of space, whereas conduction and convection require a material medium.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT Science textbooks — heat transfer and radiation.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT Science textbooks — heat transfer and radiation

questions.q: Which enzyme in gastric juice begins the chemical digestion of proteins in the human stomach?
questions.e: Pepsin is a protease released as inactive pepsinogen and activated in the acidic stomach environment. It begins breaking proteins into smaller peptides; salivary amylase acts mainly on starch rather than protein.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT Class X Science — Life Processes and digestion.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT Class X Science — Life Processes and digestion

questions.q: Why does a clear daytime sky usually appear blue to an observer on Earth?
o: The oceans reflect blue light uniformly into the atmosphere
Ozone emits blue light during daylight
Air molecules scatter shorter visible wavelengths more strongly than longer wavelengths
Cloud droplets absorb every colour except blue
questions.e: Air molecules scatter shorter visible wavelengths more strongly than longer wavelengths. This wavelength-dependent process is called Rayleigh scattering, which sends more blue light across the sky; the colour is not simply reflected from oceans.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT Class X Science — Human Eye and the Colourful World.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT Class X Science — Human Eye and the Colourful World

questions.q: A species whose effect on ecosystem structure is disproportionately large compared with its abundance is known as a:
questions.e: A keystone species has an ecological effect much greater than its abundance would suggest. Its removal can reorganise food webs or habitat structure and cause major community changes; endemic describes geographic restriction instead.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. U.S. National Park Service — biodiversity glossary and keystone species.

questions.q: Primary ecological succession on newly exposed bare rock usually begins with which pioneer organisms?
questions.e: Primary succession starts where soil is absent, such as newly exposed rock. Lichens can colonise bare surfaces, help weather the rock and add organic matter, supporting gradual soil formation and the establishment of later plant communities.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. OpenStax Concepts of Biology — community ecology and succession.

questions.sourceName: OpenStax Concepts of Biology — community ecology and succession

questions.q: A non-native species spreads rapidly in a new region and causes ecological or economic harm. It is best described as:
questions.e: An alien species is introduced beyond its natural range; it is considered invasive when its introduction or spread threatens biodiversity, ecosystem functioning or human interests. Not every non-native species is automatically invasive.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Convention on Biological Diversity — invasive alien species.

questions.q: Which example represents ex-situ conservation rather than in-situ conservation?
o: A national park protecting wildlife in its natural habitat
A seed bank preserving plant genetic material outside its natural habitat
A biosphere reserve conserving an ecosystem
A sacred grove protected in its original location
questions.e: Ex-situ conservation protects organisms or genetic material outside their natural habitats, for example in seed banks, botanical gardens and zoos. National parks, biosphere reserves and sacred groves conserve species in situ, within their ecosystems.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Convention on Biological Diversity — Article 9, Ex-situ Conservation.

questions.topic: Meghalaya Biodiversity Governance — People's Biodiversity Register
questions.q: Under India's biodiversity framework, what is the principal documentary function of a People's Biodiversity Register prepared by a Biodiversity Management Committee?
o: Record local biological resources and associated traditional knowledge
List only species already declared extinct worldwide
Record every wildlife offence registered by the police
Register only commercially imported crop varieties
questions.e: A People's Biodiversity Register documents biological resources found in the local area and associated traditional knowledge. It supports local biodiversity documentation and planning; it is not a police register or merely a list of imported crop varieties.

questions.q: In a group of 60 candidates, 35 know Excel, 28 know Word and 12 know both. How many candidates know neither Excel nor Word?
questions.e: By inclusion–exclusion, candidates knowing at least one = 35 + 28 − 12 = 51. Those knowing neither = 60 − 51 = 9. Subtract the overlap once because it was counted in both groups.

questions.q: A candidate is ranked 12th from the top and 19th from the bottom in a merit list. How many candidates are in the list?
questions.e: The candidate is counted in both rank positions, so subtract one duplicate: total = rank from top + rank from bottom − 1 = 12 + 19 − 1 = 30. Adding the two ranks without subtracting one would count the candidate twice.

questions.topic: Deductive Logic — Switch and Bulb Puzzle
questions.q: Three switches are outside a closed room. Exactly one controls a working incandescent bulb inside. You may operate the switches as you wish but may enter the room only once. The bulb becomes warm when it is on. Which method identifies the correct switch?
o: Turn all three switches on together, then enter and identify the hottest switch
Turn switch 1 on and enter immediately; if the bulb is off, switch 2 is correct
Turn switch 1 on for several minutes, turn it off, turn switch 2 on, then enter: lit means 2, warm but unlit means 1, cold and unlit means 3
Turn switch 1 and switch 2 on together, then turn both off before entering
questions.e: Switch 1 leaves residual heat after being turned off; switch 2 leaves the bulb lit; switch 3 leaves it cold and unlit. Entering once lets you use both light and residual heat to distinguish all three switches.
tags: Deductive Logic — Switch and Bulb Puzzle

questions.q: A system follows this rule: if the server is down, the dashboard is unavailable. The dashboard is currently available. Which conclusion must follow from the rule?
o: No conclusion about the server is possible
questions.e: The rule states that server down implies dashboard unavailable. Because the dashboard is available, the antecedent cannot be true. This is modus tollens: if P implies Q and Q is false, infer that P is false.

questions.q: A balance scale has three possible outcomes in each weighing: left heavier, right heavier or balance. Exactly one of several identical-looking balls is heavier. What is the maximum number of balls from which the heavier one can always be identified in two weighings?
questions.e: Divide nine balls into three groups of three and weigh two groups. If balanced, the heavier ball is in the third group; otherwise it is in the heavier group. A second weighing of two balls identifies it. Two three-outcome weighings distinguish at most 3² = 9 cases.

questions.q: A cube is painted on all six faces and cut into 27 identical smaller cubes. How many smaller cubes have exactly two painted faces?
questions.e: Small cubes with exactly two painted faces lie at the middle of each edge, excluding the corner cubes. A cube has 12 edges, and a 3 × 3 × 3 division contributes one such middle cube per edge, giving 12.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Original reasoning problem; independently constructed and solution-checked for Meghalaya PSC aptitude practice.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Original reasoning problem; independently constructed and solution-checked for Meghalaya PSC aptitude practice

questions.q: Three boxes contain only red balls, only blue balls, or a mixture of both. Their labels are 'Red', 'Blue' and 'Mixed', but every label is wrong. A ball drawn from the box labelled 'Mixed' is red. What must that box contain?
questions.e: Because every label is wrong, the box marked Mixed cannot contain both colours. Drawing a red ball proves it contains red; therefore it must be the all-red box. The contents of the other two boxes can then be resolved by elimination.

questions.topic: Truth-Teller Logic — Exactly One True Statement
questions.q: Exactly one of A, B and C tells the truth. A says, 'B is lying.' B says, 'C is lying.' C says, 'A and B are both lying.' Who tells the truth?
questions.e: If A were truthful, B would be lying; that would make C truthful, whose claim would then force A to be lying, a contradiction. If B is truthful, C is lying and A is lying, so exactly one statement is true: B.
tags: Truth-Teller Logic — Exactly One True Statement

questions.q: The duties of the clerk include preparing the monthly return, checking the ledger and ___ notices to taxpayers.
questions.e: The three duties must use parallel grammatical forms: preparing, checking and issuing. Each item in the list is a gerund. Mixing in an infinitive or a past-tense verb breaks the parallel structure.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Purdue OWL — Parallel Structure.

questions.q: The committee recommended that every applicant ___ the prescribed form personally.
questions.e: After verbs such as recommend, insist or suggest, formal English often uses the mandative subjunctive: subject + base form of the verb. Therefore 'that every applicant submit' is correct even though the subject is singular.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. British Council LearnEnglish — Reporting verbs and that-clauses.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: British Council LearnEnglish — Reporting verbs and that-clauses

questions.q: Choose the revision that removes the dangling modifier from this sentence: 'After reviewing the file, the discrepancy was corrected by the clerk.'
o: After reviewing the file, the discrepancy corrected the clerk.
The discrepancy, after reviewing the file, was corrected.
After reviewing the file, the clerk corrected the discrepancy.
The clerk corrected, after the file reviewing, the discrepancy.
questions.e: The introductory phrase 'After reviewing the file' must describe the person who reviewed it. In the original, 'discrepancy' appears to be the reviewer. Making 'the clerk' the subject removes the dangling modifier.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Purdue OWL — Dangling Modifiers and How to Correct Them.

questions.sourceName: Purdue OWL — Dangling Modifiers and How to Correct Them

questions.q: The officer objected to ___ the records before the inspection.
questions.e: In 'objected to', the word 'to' is a preposition, not part of an infinitive. A preposition is followed by a noun or a gerund, so 'objected to destroying' is correct.

questions.q: The audit team will ___ the unexplained difference before signing the report.
questions.e: 'Look into' means investigate or examine the cause of something. 'Look after' means care for, 'look up' means search for information, and 'look out' means be alert.

questions.q: The files belong to several officers. Which phrase correctly expresses this plural possession?
questions.e: For a regular plural noun ending in -s, form the possessive by adding only an apostrophe: officers'. The singular possessive is officer's, so 'the officers' files' means files belonging to several officers.

questions.topic: Number Theory — Trailing Zeroes in a Factorial
questions.q: How many trailing zeroes are there in 100! (100 factorial)?
questions.e: Each factor of 5 in 100! pairs with a factor of 2 to create a trailing zero. Count multiples of 5 and the extra factors supplied by multiples of 25: floor(100/5) + floor(100/25) = 20 + 4 = 24.
tags: Number Theory — Trailing Zeroes in a Factorial

questions.q: A cylindrical tank has an internal radius of 2 metres and a height of 3.5 metres. What is its volume in cubic metres?
questions.e: The volume of a cylinder is πr²h. With internal radius r = 2 m and height h = 3.5 m, V = π × 2² × 3.5 = 14π m³, approximately 43.98 m³. The internal radius gives the usable capacity.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT Mathematics — mensuration reference; original calculation independently checked.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A committee of 3 members is to be selected from 8 applicants. How many distinct committees can be formed if the order of selection does not matter?
questions.e: Order does not matter for a committee, so use combinations: 8C3 = 8! ÷ (3! × 5!) = (8 × 7 × 6) ÷ (3 × 2 × 1) = 56. Counting arrangements would overcount the same group in different orders.

questions.q: A trapezium has parallel sides of 12 cm and 18 cm, and a perpendicular height of 7 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: Area of a trapezium = half the sum of its parallel sides multiplied by perpendicular height. Here, ½ × (12 + 18) × 7 = ½ × 30 × 7 = 105 cm².
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT Mathematics — mensuration reference; original calculation independently checked.

questions.q: A 13-metre ladder rests against a vertical wall with its foot 5 metres from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
questions.e: The wall, ground and ladder form a right triangle. By Pythagoras, height² + 5² = 13², so height² = 169 − 25 = 144 and height = 12 metres.

questions.topic: Statistics — Median of an Odd-Sized Dataset
questions.q: Find the median of the numbers 7, 12, 9, 15, 10, 14 and 8.
questions.e: First arrange the values in ascending order: 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14, 15. With seven observations, the fourth value is the middle observation and therefore the median: 10.

questions.q: At a divergent plate boundary, two neighbouring lithospheric plates move away from each other. Which process commonly forms new oceanic crust there?
o: Subduction of one plate beneath the other
Horizontal sliding along a transform fault
Seafloor spreading as magma rises and solidifies
questions.e: At a divergent boundary, plates move apart and mantle-derived magma rises into the gap. It cools and solidifies to form new oceanic crust. Subduction and collision are associated with convergent boundaries, while transform boundaries slide past one another.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. U.S. Geological Survey — Understanding plate tectonics.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: El Niño refers to an unusual warming of which ocean region?
o: The central and eastern equatorial Pacific
questions.e: El Niño is the warm phase of the El Niño–Southern Oscillation and is marked by unusual sea-surface warming in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific. It is not a warming of the Indian, Mediterranean or Arctic Ocean.

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes TCP from UDP in computer networking?
o: UDP always guarantees delivery and ordering, while TCP does not
Both protocols require a prior connection and provide identical error control
TCP is connection-oriented and supports reliable, ordered delivery; UDP is connectionless and does not guarantee delivery
TCP is used only for email, while UDP is used only for web pages
questions.e: TCP establishes a connection and uses sequencing, acknowledgements and retransmission to support reliable ordered delivery. UDP sends datagrams without a connection and does not itself guarantee delivery or order, which reduces protocol overhead.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NIELIT — networking and Internet protocols study material.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NIELIT — networking and Internet protocols study material

questions.q: What is the main functional difference between an intrusion detection system (IDS) and an intrusion prevention system (IPS)?
o: An IDS detects and alerts; an IPS can also take action to block or prevent detected activity
An IDS encrypts files; an IPS assigns IP addresses
An IDS replaces a router; an IPS replaces a database
An IDS prevents all attacks automatically, while an IPS only records them
questions.e: An IDS monitors traffic or events and raises alerts when it detects suspicious activity. An IPS is deployed to act on detections and can block or drop traffic automatically. Neither system guarantees that every attack will be stopped.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NIELIT Shillong — cyber security and intrusion detection/prevention study material.

A cash-only booking service for inter-State buses
A vehicle insurance scheme restricted to government employees
A commission-free app platform for taxi, auto and two-wheeler operators

questions.q: According to the Meghalaya Government's press release of 12 November 2026, how many job openings in Shillong were announced for the first AI Job Fair?
questions.e: The Meghalaya Government's 12 November 2026 release for the first AI Job Fair in Shillong announced 125 job openings and anticipated more than 400 candidates and institutional heads. The figure is tied to that dated event announcement, not a permanent employment statistic.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Government of Meghalaya — First AI Job Fair press release (12 November 2026).

questions.q: Which three Senior National Archery Championships were hosted together in Meghalaya in November 2026?
o: 32nd NTPC Senior Indian Round, 21st NTPC Senior Compound and 45th NTPC Senior Recurve
33rd NTPC Junior Indian Round, 22nd NTPC Junior Compound and 46th NTPC Junior Recurve
33rd NTPC Senior Indian Round, 22nd NTPC Senior Compound and 46th NTPC Senior Recurve
33rd NTPC Senior Indian Round, 22nd NTPC Senior Recurve and 46th NTPC Senior Compound
questions.e: The State's 17 November 2026 release identifies the combined events as the 33rd Senior Indian Round, 22nd Senior Compound and 46th Senior Recurve championships, each under NTPC. The senior category and the event order distinguish them from junior events.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Government of Meghalaya — Medal Ceremony of the Senior National Archery Championships (17 November 2026).
